topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestReorgUnsafeHead`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed by Claude on behalf of @ajsutton.

**CI run:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/123078/workflows/4327c7d8-ab80-44a4-9508-0c99d5bc2fe0/jobs/4868463/tests

**Job:** `memory-all-kona-op-reth` (acceptance tests)
**Date:** 2026-04-21
**Branch:** `gh-readonly-queue/develop/pr-20165-4df50ca0801bf0dd7049995d5a7c8cc8396023df` (merge queue)
**Test file:** `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/reorgs/unsafe_head_test.go:113`

**Error:**
```
Error Trace: /home/circleci/project/op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/reorgs/unsafe_head_test.go:113
Error:       Should not be: 0xae78b3b90db8d7d10c044465707fc30e969695515bb3e778accb1554867a7831
Test:        TestReorgUnsafeHead
Messages:    Expected to get different heads on divergence block number, but got the same hash, so no reorg happened on chain A
```

Preceding log lines:

```
unsafe_head_test.go:111: Reorged chain A on divergence block number (prior the reorg) number=9 head=ae78b3..7a7831 parent=5aaa56..e2828e
unsafe_head_test.go:112: Reorged chain A on divergence block number (after the reorg) number=9 head=ae78b3..7a7831 parent=5aaa56..e2828e
```

**Context:**
- The test was unskipped and migrated to `TwoL2SupernodeInterop` in #20136 (commit `4df50ca080`).
- After `StopSequencer()`, the test uses `op-test-sequencer` to sequence a conflicting block at the unsafe head height, then calls `StartSequencer()` on the CL and waits for a new block.
- At the assertion, the block at the divergence height is still the original block — the EL's view of the unsafe head was never replaced by the test-sequencer's conflicting block (or the CL's resumed sequencing reverted the reorg).
- The test intersperses two `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` calls between `ia.New()` / `ia.Next()` at lines 97 and 101 — likely a timing race.

Will investigate and propose a fix.

topPRs.title: test: reproduce #21663 NUT bundle drift via L2DevFeatureFlags version bump
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Do not merge — diagnostic experiment for the CI failures in ethereum-optimism/optimism#21663.

**What this shows:** the karst/lagoon NUT activation failures come from the **semver downgrade guard** in `L2ContractsManagerUtils.upgradeTo` (reverts `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed` when the installed proxy version > the version the bundle installs), combined with a test-fixture gap: **L2DevFeatureFlags is not captured in any pre-fork state file**, so the NUT activation test rebuilds it from HEAD instead of the fork era.

- Before: HEAD L2DevFeatureFlags = 1.0.0, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.0,1.0.0)=false` → pass.
- After the bump: HEAD = 1.0.1, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.1,1.0.0)=true` → downgrade → revert.

Commits:
1. bump L2DevFeatureFlags semver 1.0.0 → 1.0.1
2. comment-only touch to the NUT test file (contracts-only changes don't set `rust_changes_detected`, so the NUT test would be skipped — a CI gap in its own right)
3. regenerate `current-upgrade-bundle.json`
4. regenerate `semver-lock.json`
5. bump the version unit test to 1.0.1 + re-snapshot the **lagoon** bundle (karst left immutable)

Expected CI after commit 5: snapshot checks + version test green; **lagoon** NUT/interop green (bundle now installs 1.0.1, matching HEAD); **karst** NUT still red (its immutable bundle installs 1.0.0 while the test's HEAD genesis has 1.0.1). Note: `nut-provenance-verify lagoon` will fail because the lock commit is the develop merge-base, which predates the change.

topPRs.title: feat(kona/derive): pure sync deriver with full span-batch overlap check (phase 3/6)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of 6 — stacked on top of #20703 (Phase 2) → #20702 (Phase 1).

Builds a pure (sync, IO-free, `no_std`) `Deriver` on top of phase 2's
`crate::core::*` primitives, and closes the post-Holocene span-batch
overlap content-check spec gap that both op-node
(`op-node/rollup/derive/batch_stage.go:139`) and kona's async pipeline
(`crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/span.rs:591`) skip today.

**Closes spec gap: full byte-wise post-Holocene span-batch overlap content check** — implemented in `pure/overlap.rs` and exercised by both unit and replay tests.

## Public API (`kona_derive::pure`)

- `Deriver::new(rollup_cfg, l1_cfg, sys_config, safe_head, dependency_set)`
- `Deriver::derive(safe_head) -> (Derivation, DeriveTrace)` — **never returns `Err`**
- `Deriver::add_l1_input(L1Input) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::add_span_batch_overlap(SpanBatchOverlap) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::reset(safe_head, sys_config) -> DeriveTrace`
- `extract_l1_input(header, txs, receipts, rollup_cfg) -> L1Input` — **filter-only, sysconfig-blind**

`Derivation` variants the caller matches exhaustively:
- `Attributes { attrs }` — emit and advance the engine.
- `NeedL1Input` — fetch + extract + `add_l1_input`.
- `NeedSpanBatchOverlap { parent, content }` — fetch L2 range + `add_span_batch_overlap`.

## Contract invariants

Encoded in the types and verified by tests:

- `derive` never errors. Malformed frames / channels / batches / deposit logs / config logs surface as typed `TraceEntry::*Dropped` / `*Failed` entries.
- `add_*` only error on contract violations (`NonContiguousL1Input`, `L1InputParentMismatch`, `UnsolicitedOverlap`, `OverlapParentMismatch`, `OverlapRangeMismatch`).
- No `tracing::*` calls inside `pure/`. Callers translate `DeriveTrace` entries.
- `extract_l1_input` does no fallible parsing; `L1Input` carries raw `Vec<Log>` and `Vec<(Address, Bytes)>`.
- `extract_l1_input` does **not** accept a `SystemConfig`; the dynamic `batcher_addr` filter lives in the deriver (sysconfig-blind helper).
- `SpanBatchOverlapBlock.txs: Vec<Bytes>` — raw RLP throughout, no encode/decode round-trip in the overlap check.
- `pure/` is `no_std`; verified by `--target=riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf`.
- Every `match` on `Derivation` and `TraceEntry` inside `pure/` is exhaustive; strict typed reason enums everywhere, no `String` reason fields.
- `reset(safe_head, sys_config)` clears pending channels, decoded-but-un-emitted batches, active overlap state, and the L1 input buffer; supplied `sys_config` becomes the new rolling sysconfig.

## Verification gates

All run from `rust/`:

- `cargo build -p kona-derive --no-default-features` — **PASS**
- `cargo build -p kona-derive --no-default-features --target=riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` — **PASS** (no_std proof)
- `cargo build -p kona-derive` (default) — **PASS**
- `cargo test -p kona-derive --lib pure::` — **20/20 PASS** (both with and without default features)
- `cargo test -p kona-derive --test replay` — **3/3 PASS**
- `cargo clippy -p kona-derive --all-targets -- -D warnings` — **CLEAN**
- `cargo clippy -p kona-derive --no-default-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — **CLEAN**

Full lib-test result: **250 passed, 1 failed**. The single failure is the pre-existing flake `test_span_batch_extraction_error_flushes_stage` (a `tracing` global-default subscriber collision that reproduces on the phase 2 baseline). Not introduced by this PR.

Downstream consumers (`kona-node-service`, `kona-proof`, `kona-driver`) compile cleanly against the new surface.

## Replay test — synthetic fixtures

The replay test at `crates/protocol/derive/tests/replay.rs` uses **synthetic** fixtures rather than recorded mainnet data. Recording a real mainnet fixture requires both an L1 RPC and a beacon-chain endpoint covering the chosen range plus an L2 lookup snapshot — not available in the environment this PR was assembled in.

The synthetic fixtures hit each load-bearing code path the plan calls out:

- `replay_hardfork_activation_boundary` — feeds an L1 stream straddling a Granite activation timestamp and asserts the deriver continues without any soft-reset signal. This closes the otherwise-hidden risk that the deleted `Signal::Activation` site (`actor.rs:130` in kona-node) was load-bearing — the hard gate the plan names before phase 4 can proceed.
- `replay_sysconfig_and_deposit_paths` — feeds a real `ConfigUpdate` log and a real `TransactionDeposited` log alongside malformed versions of each, and asserts the deriver emits exactly one `SystemConfigUpdated`, one `SystemConfigUpdateDropped`, and one `DepositLogDropped`.
- `replay_long_empty_sequence_stays_quiet` — sanity check: 40 empty L1 blocks produce no spurious drops.

`crates/protocol/derive/tests/fixtures/README.md` documents the synthetic-vs-real situation, what would be needed to record real fixtures, and how the future `record-fixtures` cargo feature will be wired so CI replays from frozen bytes only.

## Unit test coverage

Per-component tests asserting specific `TraceEntry` shapes (no log-grep):

- `pure::extract::tests` (4) — batch-inbox filter, deposit log filter, config log filter, failed-receipt skip.
- `pure::overlap::tests` (5) — accept-on-full-match, drop on tx-count mismatch / tx mismatch / l1-origin mismatch / missing L1 info tx.
- `pure::deriver::tests` (11) — empty path, non-contiguous L1 error, parent-mismatch error, unsolicited-overlap error, reset clears state + emits `Reset` event, malformed sysconfig log → `SystemConfigUpdateDropped`, malformed deposit log → `DepositLogDropped`, batcher-from mismatch → `BatchInboxTxIgnoredFromMismatch`, garbage calldata → `FramesParseFailed`, sequencing-window expiry → `EmptyBatchGenerated`, future-safe-head sanity.

Total: 20 unit + 3 replay = 23 new tests, all passing.

## Files

- `crates/protocol/derive/src/lib.rs` — wire up `pure::*`; hoist test macros out of `test_utils/` so `--no-default-features` lib tests can construct frames.
- `crates/protocol/derive/src/pure/` — new module: `deriver.rs`, `types.rs`, `extract.rs`, `overlap.rs`, `mod.rs`.
- `crates/protocol/derive/src/stages/traversal/{indexed,polling}.rs` — minor clippy fix (`const fn` for `update_origin`), unblocks `clippy -D warnings`.
- `crates/protocol/derive/src/test_macros.rs` — moved from `test_utils/macros.rs` so the `frame!` macro is available without `feature = "async"`.
- `crates/protocol/derive/tests/replay.rs` — new replay test.
- `crates/protocol/derive/tests/fixtures/README.md` — documents synthetic vs. recorded fixtures.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20698
Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20695

topPRs.title: feat(kona-sp1): scaffold super interop programs
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the initial SP1 super interop proof shape for ZK dispute games.

It introduces shared public IO types for the unified super-range program and final super-aggregation program, including super-root encoding and final public-value encoding that match the tuple verified by `ZKDisputeGame.prove`.

The output-root range and consolidation proofs are now handled by a single unified super-range program with (optimistic output-root) range and consolidation modes, so aggregation verifies one semantic class of proof with one `range_vkey`.

The guest execution logic is intentionally still incomplete in this PR. The aggregation program accepts the range vkey dynamically for now, and the range/consolidation verification bodies are left as TODOs for the follow-up implementation work.

## Program Input Validation

This PR also introduces logic to validate the program input shape. This validation is complementary to the more involved super-STF operations, ensuring that the super-aggregation program verifies that all required proofs are well-formed and provided.

### Super-range input validation

The unified super-range program first validates the mode-specific input shape.
For range mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- chain IDs are non-empty and strictly increasing
- claimed transitions cover exactly every (timestamp, chain_id) pair in span order
- each transition’s timestamp and chain ID match the expected position

For consolidation mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- there is one consolidation input per timestamp
- each claimed super-root proof has the expected timestamp
- each super-root proof uses the supported version and ordered chain set
- optimistic blocks are non-empty, strictly ordered, and match the claimed super-root proof’s chain coverage
- every timestamp uses the same chain set

### Super-aggregation input validation

Aggregation validates the declared range public outputs before recursive proof verification.
It checks:

- `starting_super_root_proof` hashes to `starting_root_hash`
- there is at least one range output and one consolidation output
- the disputed interval starts at `starting_super_root.timestamp + 1`
- consolidation outputs cover the full timestamp interval contiguously
- consolidation `previous_super_root` values chain forward from `starting_root_hash`
- the final consolidated root equals `root_claim`
- range outputs cover the same full timestamp interval contiguously
- every range output commits to the same `l1_head` as the game
- every range output’s `previous_super_root` matches the super root before that range
- range optimistic blocks match the corresponding consolidation optimistic blocks timestamp by timestamp
- all range/consolidation outputs use the chain set from the starting super root

## Meta

part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21459
